rows.label: Concept
rows.text: **Resonance** exists where one Lewis structure is not enough: the molecule is a **hybrid of canonical forms** that differ only in electron placement — **electrons move, atoms never do** — and the hybrid is stabilised by the **resonance energy** (benzene ≈150 kJ/mol).…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - Ozone: ⁻O–O⁺=O ↔ O=O⁺–O⁻ - Benzene: Kekulé I ↔ Kekulé II; all C–C = 1.39 Å - Resonance energy of benzene ≈ 150 kJ/mol - +R: −OH, −OR, −NH₂, −NR₂, −X; −R: −NO₂, −CN, −CHO, −COOH

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Covers only: resonance effect, -r effect (within Fundamental Principles of Organic Chemistry).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Chemistry — don't mix them.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "Resonance is the representation of a molecule as a hybrid of canonical structures differing only in electron arrangement; the resonance effect transmits electron donation (+R) or withdrawal (−R) through a conjugated pi system."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The halogen's double life*** — chlorine withdraws by induction yet donates by resonance: the combination deactivates the ring but still directs incoming groups to ortho and para — two effects, one substituent.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — When One Structure Is Not Enough Some molecules refuse to be drawn once. **Benzene** has no ordinary alternating bonds; **ozone** has two identical bonds that single-bond/double-bond pictures cannot both describe. **Resonance** solves this: the real molecule is a **hybrid** of several valid structures (**canonical forms**), differing only in electron placement.…  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Resonance — the concept - When a single Lewis structure cannot represent a molecule, the molecule is written as a **hybrid of two or more canonical structures** connected by double-headed arrows (↔).…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Rules: electrons move, atoms don't; arrow <->. Ozone: -O-O+=O <-> O=O+-O-. Benzene: two Kekule forms. +R: OH, OR, NH2, halogens (o/p); -R: NO2, CN, CHO, COOH (meta). Resonance energy benzene ~150 kJ/mol.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Delocalisation is stabilisation: electrons spread over more atoms lower the energy — benzene's 150 kJ/mol of resonance energy is why it substitutes instead of adding.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Resonance: molecule represented as hybrid of canonical structures differing only in electron placement (pi/lone pairs move; atoms fixed); real structure more stable; resonance energy benzene ~150 kJ/mol. Ozone: -O-O+=O <-> O=O+-O- (bonds identical).…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Extended conjugation from resonance is the physics of colour: longer delocalised pi systems absorb visible light, which is why dyes and beta-carotene are chains of alternating bonds.

rows.text: Contrast the resonance effect with the inductive effect in four respects.  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **Resonance is not equilibrium:** the molecule does not flip between structures; it is **one hybrid** all the time. ⇌ is wrong; ↔ is right.  ·  **Atoms never move in resonance:** only electrons shift — if you find yourself relocating an H or a group, you are drawing a different compound (a tautomer), not a canonical form.
